findings.title: Empty updateMany will throw after cache write
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Prisma rejects updateMany when data is empty, so this throws after the free/busy cache has already been written. Webhook and cache-refresh paths that reach this method will fail, and the timestamp the comment says it is updating never changes.

findings.title: Delete cache leaves Google watches running
findings.body: deleteCacheHandler only deletes CalendarCache rows after confirming the credential belongs to the caller. It does not stop the Google channel subscriptions stored on SelectedCalendar (googleChannelId / resourceId). Active watches will call fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache and immediately rewrite the cache, so "Delete cached data" does not stick and the UI can show a fresh timestamp again on the next refresh.

findings.title: Cache delete does not refresh calendar query
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. After a successful delete the dropdown still shows the previous cache_last_updated until something else refetches, so the action looks like it failed.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared tsx
findings.body: dev:cron was changed from ts-node to npx tsx cron-tester.ts, but tsx is not a dependency of @calcom/web (ts-node still is). Under Yarn 3, npx will try to fetch tsx outside the lockfile and fail offline or in CI, so the cron tester script no longer runs reliably.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only
findings.body: The script rewrites GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with sed -i '' (BSD sed). GNU sed on Linux treats the empty string as the script and errors, so the helper cannot update .env on Linux even when Tunnelmole starts successfully.
